Title: Continuous versus intermittent use of furosemide in patients with heart failure and moderate chronic renal dysfunction
Author: Zhigui Zheng et al.
Comment: Table 2 explicitly labels the variability values as SEM, so 1.01 and 0.73 were recorded as SE rather than SD. The table's arm sizes (CI n=42; BI n=39) are the final analysed sample after exclusions and were used for this outcome. For synthesis, convert SEM to SD using SD = SEM × sqrt(n). The arm-level means are already positive kilograms lost. No M_diff was stored because the paper did not explicitly report one and the group order follows the paper (CI first), while the synthesis requires CI minus BI.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('6-hour continuous intravenous furosemide infusion (CI)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False); treatment SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n)); control SD derived from its reported SE (SD = SE * sqrt(n))
Design Type: Prospective randomized controlled parallel-group clinical trial
domain: Acute decompensated heart failure with moderate chronic renal insufficiency

Title: Continuous Versus Bolus Dosing of Furosemide for Patients Hospitalized for Heart Failure
Author: Allen et al.
Comment: The paper reports signed mean weight changes of -1.64 kg (bolus) and -2.66 kg (continuous). Signs were reversed per the synthesis contract so weight loss is positive: 1.64 and 2.66 kg. M_diff was computed as continuous minus bolus: 2.66 - 1.64 = 1.02 kg. Table-header randomized group sizes were used; the paper states intention-to-treat analysis, 100% follow-up at discharge, and no protocol violations.
Design Type: Prospective open-label single-center parallel-group randomized controlled trial
domain: Acute decompensated heart failure; intravenous loop-diuretic dosing
Study Environment: Duke University Medical Center inpatient hospital setting
Participant type: Adults hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure and volume overload
Recruitment source: Patients admitted to Duke University Medical Center from 1999 to 2005
Outcome measurement: Change in body weight from admission to hospital day 3 or earlier discharge, harmonized as positive kilograms lost
effect_direction: Continuous infusion minus bolus; positive MD means greater weight loss and favors continuous infusion.

Title: Increased mortality in elderly heart failure patients receiving infusion of furosemide compared to elderly heart failure patients receiving bolus injection

Title: Diuretic Strategies in Patients with Acute Decompensated Heart Failure
Author: Felker et al.
Comment: The paper reports negative weight changes in pounds; values were sign-reversed to positive weight loss and divided by 2.205 per the synthesis contract: bolus mean 6.8/2.205=3.08 kg and SD 7.8/2.205=3.54 kg; continuous mean 8.1/2.205=3.67 kg and SD 10.3/2.205=4.67 kg. Outcome-specific analyzed Ns were not reported, so randomized arm sizes from the Table 2 headers were used. These are administration-mode marginal groups from a 2-by-2 factorial trial, so M_diff was left null under the stated prohibition on computing it from factorial marginal means.
Design Type: Prospective double-blind double-dummy randomized controlled 2-by-2 factorial trial
Participant type: Adults hospitalized with acute decompensated heart failure
Recruitment source: 26 clinical sites in the United States and Canada
Outcome measurement: Change in body weight at 72 hours, sign-reversed so weight loss is positive and converted from pounds to kilograms
effect_direction: Continuous infusion minus bolus; positive MD means greater weight loss and favors continuous infusion.

Author: Yayla et al.
Comment: The paper does not explicitly report the number analyzed for body-weight loss, so randomized group sizes (cIV n=15; bI n=14) were used. The p=0.66 value is the omnibus three-group test including HSS, not a pairwise cIV-versus-bI p value.
